title: CD contracts, operator checklist, and canary decision tree (quickdraft)
summary: Working draft: lightweight CD contracts for on-prem/VPC operator integration, an operator checklist for safe rollouts, and a compact canary decision tree for automated rollbacks and manual handoff triggers.
body:
Purpose:
This document is a pragmatic, short-form reference for teams integrating the Redwood operator and Argo-based GitOps workflows into customer private deployments. Goal is to define minimal CD contracts (inputs/outputs), a checklist for operator authors and SREs, and a deterministic canary decision tree that spans automated signals and manual intervention checkpoints.

Background/context:
- Many private-deploy customers run an operator (Helm + CRDs) that materializes Argo Applications and node workloads.
- We need a small, stable contract between the CI pipeline, TF modules (provisioning), and the operator to avoid mismatched expectations during upgrades.
- Focus: image promotion, attestation verification, helm values compatibility, and safe rollback/hand-off procedures.

1) CD contract (minimal, machine-readable fields) - this is the shape CI and TF should agree on:
- artifact_reference: string (oci uri, e.g. registry.company.io/redwood/inference:sha256-<short>)
- attestation_uri: string (cosign attestation blob or SLSA predicate location)
- sbom_uri: string (optional)
- semver_tag: string (optional; used for human-facing release notes)
- required_helm_values_checksum: string (sha256 of canonicalized relevant values for this operator release)
- tf_release_id: string (unique id from terraform apply for the cluster / operator bundle)
- allowed_rollout_modes: list ("canary", "immediate", "manual") - pipeline and operator must agree on permitted modes
- max_concurrent_canaries: number-as-string (e.g. "3")

Implementation notes:
- Keep contract as a small JSON blob emitted by CI after a successful build + attestation. Put the blob into the artifact registry and pass the URI to TF and Argo via ApplicationSources.
- The operator validates attestation and checks the values checksum before allowing the Argo Application to sync. If mismatch -> block and emit a clear error with remediation steps.

2) Terraform module interface (recommended inputs / outputs) - keep plain keys so other teams can call the module without deep coupling:
Inputs (module parameters):
- cluster_id (string)
- operator_version (string)
- allowed_rollout_modes (list)
- registry_creds_secret (string)
- monitoring_namespace (string)
- argo_appset_config (string / yaml blob)
- preflight_checks_enabled (bool-as-string)
- image_attestation_policy_id (string)
Outputs:
- operator_service_account_name (string)
- argo_appset_url (string)
body_continued:
- tf_release_id (string)
- preflight_report_s3_uri (string)

Notes:
- TF module should not bake image URIs; CI is the single source of truth for artifact URIs and attestations. TF references the artefact blob produced by CI.
- Expose a preflight_report_s3_uri so UI/console can surface preflight problems to customers.

3) Operator checklist (for operator authors + SREs) - lightweight and actionable
- [ ] Validate attestation: reject images without a valid cosign predicate or signed SLSA assertion.
- [ ] Canonicalize helm values for checksum comparison (strip comments, order maps).
- [ ] Emit a blocking condition on the CRD if checksum or attestation fails, with a link to remediation steps.
- [ ] Implement a "quarantine" namespace for images failing attestation for audit and manual review.
- [ ] Respect allowed_rollout_modes: operator must not start canaries if mode is "manual".
- [ ] Expose rollout status in k8s conditions and push events to the customer event sink (if configured).
- [ ] Telemetry hooks: emit events on canary start, canary pass/fail, automatic rollback, and manual takeover. Attach trace ids from Argo/CI to correlate.
- [ ] Safe defaults: conservative canary sizes (1-2% of pods by default) and conservative traffic ramping.

4) Canary decision tree (compact, deterministic)
- Preconditions before canary starts:
  a) attestation and checksum validated -> OK to start
  b) preflight smoke test result == PASS -> OK to start
  c) monitoring baseline collected -> OK to start

- Canary start -> evaluation window (configured, e.g. 10m) -> evaluate signals:
  Signals evaluated (priority order):
  1) Critical crashloop / pod OOMs (if > 0.5% of canary pods crash in window) -> FAIL -> immediate rollback
  2) Error rate increase (api error rate) relative to baseline > 3x and absolute increase > 0.5% -> FAIL -> rollback
  3) P95 latency regression compared to baseline > 2x and delta > 300ms -> FAIL -> rollback or pause for manual review (if manual_review configured)
  4) Token usage cost delta > +50% -> FAIL -> pause and route to cost owner review
  5) No signal degradation for entire window -> PASS -> promote to ramp (next bucket)

- Ramp policy:
  - Each ramp step doubles traffic up to a configured max percentage. Between steps wait for evaluation window.
  - If a step fails, run automatic rollback and notify owner channel with links to logs and sagas.

- Manual takeover:
  - If operator sees an ambiguous but serious signal (e.g., minor latency increase but high user impact), it should set a "requires_manual_review" condition and pause the rollout. That triggers a Slack/Email/Jira alert with playbook link.

5) CI pipeline example (high level steps; intentionally implementation-agnostic)
- build -> run unit + integration smoke tests (local) -> container image push -> generate sbom & cosign attestation -> run preflight suite against a short-lived preview cluster -> generate preflight report + artifact_contract.json (contains contract fields above) -> PR: attach artifact_contract.json + links -> merge -> create promotion PR to infra (which references artifact blob) -> TF apply (creates/updates operator + argo app) -> operator validates and Argo syncs -> canary rollout triggered by Argo rollout controller.

6) Observability and alerts (what to ship with every operator release)
- metrics: canary_count, canary_failures_total, canary_rollbacks_total, last_canary_reason{reason}, preflight_failures_total.
- logs: structured event on canary start/end with fields: artifact_reference, trace_id, canary_id, step_metrics (p95, error_rate).
- alerts: immediate page on automatic rollback OR if preflight failures > threshold for last 24h.

7) Clear remediation messages (UX detail)
- When a CI artifact is blocked by checksum mismatch: provide both the canonical helm-values.yaml used to compute checksum and a remediation checklist (how to re-run CI to rebuild the artifact). Avoid opaque "checksum mismatch" errors.
- When attestation fails: include attestation id and link to the predicate content and signer key id.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want to require SBOMs for all private deploys or only for regulated customers? (Priya to own recommendation)
- Finalize conservative default thresholds for error-rate and latency (SRE + product decision).
- Decide whether TF should attempt to auto-update allowed_rollout_modes from CI metadata or strictly read-from-operator-config (security tradeoffs).

Appendix: sample minimal artifact_contract.json (human readable example)
{
  "artifact_reference": "registry.corp/redwood/inference:sha256-abcdef",
  "attestation_uri": "oci://registry.corp/attestations/sha256-abcdef:predicate",
  "sbom_uri": "s3://redwood-artifacts/sbom/sha256-abcdef.json",
  "required_helm_values_checksum": "sha256:1234abcd",
  "tf_release_id": "tf-r-20251105-009",
  "allowed_rollout_modes": ["canary", "manual"]
}

Quick next steps:
- Share with operator authors and SREs for first-pass feedback (diego, owen).
- Iterate on preflight suite and attach to the CI pipeline PR that produces artifact_contract.json.
- Create a small test harness (k6 + synthetic traffic + canary runner) that operators can use to validate decision tree thresholds in staging.

Notes-to-self: keep the contract fuzzy enough to evolve but small enough to be machine readable and verifiable.
